items.stem: A loop keeps running and never stops. Which description names this problem?

options.text: An infinite loop caused by a condition that never becomes false
options.rationale: Correct: the loop condition is never made false, so the loop never ends.

options.text: A syntax error that stops the program compiling
options.rationale: A syntax error prevents the program from running at all; this program runs but will not stop.

options.text: A type mismatch between two variables
options.rationale: A type mismatch is unrelated to whether the loop terminates.

options.text: A missing return value from a procedure
options.rationale: A missing return value does not by itself cause a loop to run forever.

items.explanation: Correct: the loop condition is never made false, so the loop never ends.

items.stem: Which of the following are good reasons to break a program into procedures? (Select TWO)

options.text: Each piece of logic can be named, reused and tested on its own
options.rationale: Correct: procedures let you name, reuse and test a unit of logic independently.

options.text: It removes the need to decompose the problem first
options.rationale: Decomposition is what leads you to the procedures; it is not replaced by them.

options.text: Repeated steps can be written once and called many times
options.rationale: Correct: shared logic lives in one place instead of being copied.

options.text: It guarantees the program has no bugs
options.rationale: Procedures help organise code but do not guarantee correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: procedures let you name, reuse and test a unit of logic independently.

items.stem: A program runs with no error messages but produces the wrong total. What kind of error is this?

options.rationale: Correct: the program runs but the logic produces an incorrect result.
A syntax error would stop the program from running at all.
Nothing indicates a hardware fault; the symptom is a wrong computed value.
The program produced an output, so input was received; the fault is in the logic.

items.explanation: Correct: the program runs but the logic produces an incorrect result.
